steps.body: Every amount has a **number symbol**. Three dots is written **3**. Ten dots is written **10**.

widget.prompt: How many dots? Pick the number.

commonPicks.feedback: There was one more. The number is 2.
One fewer than that. The number is 2.

widget.successFeedback: Yes — the symbol 2 means two dots!

steps.body: **Zero** — written **0** — means **none at all**. An empty plate has 0 cookies.

explanationVariants: An empty frame has no dots — that amount is written 0.

widget.prompt: A ten-frame has no dots in it. Which number tells how many dots?

options.feedback: Yes! No dots at all means zero — written 0.
1 means one dot. This frame has NONE — that is 0.
10 would be a FULL frame. Empty means 0.
5 means five dots. An empty frame holds 0.

widget.prompt: The number is 6. Tap that many dots.

commonCounts.feedback: The symbol 6 needs one more dot.
That is 7 — one too many for the symbol 6.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents read numerals.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for read numerals must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines read numerals.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: The symbol 9 means nine things — count 1 through 9.

widget.prompt: How many dots? Pick the matching number.

commonPicks.feedback: One cell more was filled. It was 9.
One cell was empty — not a full ten. It was 9.

widget.missFeedback: Nine fills the frame except one cell: 9.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — 9! One less than a full frame.

explanationVariants: A full ten-frame holds exactly ten dots — written 10.

widget.prompt: The frame is completely full. How many dots? Pick the number.

commonPicks.feedback: 9 leaves one empty cell. FULL means 10.
5 fills only one row. The whole frame is 10.
0 means empty. A FULL frame is 10.

widget.missFeedback: Count the cells: two rows of five make 10.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — a full frame is ten dots, written 10.

explanationVariants: Three plates: 2 cookies, 0 cookies, 1 cookie. The empty plate is the 0.
The plate with none shows zero.

widget.prompt: Ben has 3 plates. Tap the plate that shows 0 cookies.

hotspots.label: Plate with 2 cookies
hotspots.feedback: That plate shows 2. Zero means NONE.

hotspots.label: Plate with 1 cookie
hotspots.feedback: That plate shows 1. Zero means NONE.

widget.missFeedback: An empty plate shows exactly 0 — zero is a real number! Find the plate with no cookies.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — none at all is zero, written 0.

hints: Find the plate with no cookies.

steps.body: Numbers 0 to 10 are symbols for amounts. Zero means none.
takeaways: Each amount has a number symbol: 3 means three.
steps.teaser: Next: counting forward from any number.

concept.body: A number symbol tells an amount. 4 means four dots. 0 means none at all.

widget.prompt: How many dots? Pick the number.
widget.missFeedback: A row of 5 and 2 more is 7.
